doc.title: Mark Soskin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 17, 2021

title: Why he gets so many sideman calls; versatility and attitude
summary: Soskin attributes the near hundred sideman credits to doing many kinds of music and tells students to be open to club dates and all styles.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Why do you think people, I mean your list of recordings as a sideman for one thing is close to one hundred or maybe over that by now.
Yeah. How come you get all those calls? If you think about yourself as a player and as a participant do you know why people call you so often?

I do and that’s because I can do a lot of different things. You know a lot of different kinds of music I can do. And I tell that to my students, I mean the more you could do the more work you’re going to get.
Have you had students who have had a chance to play like club dates or weddings or something and they have an attitude about it? They sort of turn up their nose at, oh gee —

Well that’s not good. You know I mean if you have that attitude you’re really going to miss out on a lot of stuff. Because you’ve got to be open to different kinds of music and that’s one of the reasons I work so much.
What about the non-musical parts of the music business. How do you teach your students the importance of things like punctuality and attitude?
